title: Crash/requeue recovery strands reviews in 'pending' forever
description: cmd/drydock/main.go:111 ResetStuckReviews moves reviewing->pending at startup but nothing ever loads pending rows into processor.ReviewQueue (requeue sweep at main.go:745 only selects status='failed'). Also the sweep sets failed->pending then does a non-blocking channel send; on full channel the row is dropped with a log and is now outside all future sweeps. DB should be the work queue: workers claim pending->reviewing atomically, including at startup; channel is only a wake-up hint. Category: reliability/fake completion — recovery code that appears to recover but loses work. Files: internal/db/store.go (ResetStuckReviews, RequeueFailedReviews), cmd/drydock/main.go.
close_reason: Fixed in this session: zap receipt hardening (bolt11 required, verified 9734 correlation, fail-closed trusted zappers), DB-backed pending-review recovery (ListStalePendingReviews startup fill + sweep), verifier indeterminate tri-state with hard failure on zero valid votes, gitleaks --exit-code 0 + salvage parse, exclusion-only branch moved before fail-closed check.

title: Cashu payment can settle while review is permanently payment_blocked
description: internal/payment/service.go processTokenPayment: ambiguous/pending melt returns Reason payment_pending; pipeline converts all denials to payment_blocked:* which RequeueFailedReviews explicitly excludes (store.go:1961). No durable reconciler for submitted melts — mint may consume proofs while drydock never delivers the review. Also reconcileReservedPayment calls validateInvoiceEvidence before settlement lookup so an invoice settled before expiry can't finalize after wall-clock expiry. Category: money/reliability. Fix: distinguish terminal denial vs retryable settlement, add durable melt reconciler, allow expired invoices to finalize on proven timely settlement.
notes: Implemented explicit retryable payment_pending authorization, durable cursor-paged reconciliation of submitted/token_spent and authorized-stranded payments, atomic review requeue including legacy payment_blocked:payment_pending, post-expiry lookup with timely-settlement validation, durable terminal payment failures, and a one-minute startup/background reconciler. Terminal blocking now handles retry-sweep pending rows idempotently.
close_reason: Fixed ambiguous Cashu settlement recovery end-to-end; pending denials are retryable, durable melts reconcile and requeue reviews, and timely settlement can finalize after wall-clock expiry.

title: Forged zap receipts can authorize paid reviews (no 9734 verification, amount-tag-only accepted)
description: internal/ingest/zap.go validateZapReceipt/zapAmountMSat: with DRYDOCK_TRUSTED_ZAPPERS empty (the default, config.go:156), ANY nostr key can sign a kind-9735 event naming the service pubkey and patch event, with a bare 'amount' tag and no bolt11 invoice, and it is persisted as a valid zap receipt granting AccessZap payment authorization. No verification of the embedded kind-9734 zap request, its signature, or p/e/amount correlation; bolt11 not required. Category: security/money — fake payment path in production. Fix: require trusted zappers (or authenticated zap provider) in production config validation; require and verify signed kind-9734 description tag; correlate recipient/event/amount; require bolt11 amount match.
close_reason: Fixed in this session: zap receipt hardening (bolt11 required, verified 9734 correlation, fail-closed trusted zappers), DB-backed pending-review recovery (ListStalePendingReviews startup fill + sweep), verifier indeterminate tri-state with hard failure on zero valid votes, gitleaks --exit-code 0 + salvage parse, exclusion-only branch moved before fail-closed check.

title: marketplace: no completion or reviewer payout/settlement flow exists
description: Traced flow ends at assignment accept/reject. There is no authenticated work-submission transition, no payout destination, no invoice creation/payment, no settlement verification, and no payout ledger (internal/marketplace/router.go:213-215,493-510; internal/db/store_marketplace.go:348-367). Integration test fakes completion by writing UpdateAssignmentStatus directly (integration_test.go:243-246). A paid listing can never pay its reviewer. Category: missing-impl / money. Fix: authenticated completion event tied to assigned reviewer+patch, then transactional payout state machine (pending, submitted, settled, failed) with NWC payment, idempotency key, payment hash/preimage stored, retry/reconciliation, immutable audit records.
close_reason: Implemented authenticated marketplace/complete correlation, atomic assignment payout allocation, persisted/audited payout state machine, NWC pay_invoice plus lookup reconciliation, settlement evidence validation, concurrency/fault tests, production wiring, and passing build/targeted/full Go suites.

title: vscode extension: session announcement omits gateway p tag - IDE registration broken end-to-end
description: Extension publishes ide-session announcements with only d/type/schema/client tags (extensions/vscode-drydock/src/extension.ts:786-820), but the gateway requires hasTagValue(event.Tags, p, h.ourPubKey) (internal/idegateway/handler.go:181-183,650-661). Sessions are silently rejected so all subsequent review/fix requests fail authorization while the extension shows Ready. Category: fake-completion. Fix: add configured Drydock pubkey as a p tag on announcements; add integration test proving extension announcement passes gateway session registration.
close_reason: Added gateway p-tagged IDE announcements, verified signed gateway events and strict response correlation tags, added extension tests, and passed compile/build checks.

title: repo: path traversal in repo ID allows destructive git/file ops outside cache dir
description: safeRepoPathComponent (internal/repo/manager.go:301-312) only replaces / \ : and space; repo IDs like '..' survive and filepath.Join(baseDir, ...) escapes baseDir. Manager then runs git reset --hard, git clean -fd, checkout, and os.RemoveAll on that path (manager.go:120-139,196-205,402-446). Category: security. Fix: derive cache dir names from a cryptographic hash of the repo ID (plus safe display prefix); after joining, verify the resolved absolute path is strictly beneath baseDir before every git/filesystem operation; add tests with hostile repo IDs ('..', '.', absolute paths, control chars).
close_reason: Fixed with SHA-256 cache names, strict resolved-path containment checks, per-repo locking for ensure/fetch/cleanup/size/eviction, in-use eviction protection, and regression/concurrency tests; go build ./... and go test ./... pass.

title: Add kind-4903 audit emission on all consequential actions
description: Drydock has no kind-4903 audit emission anywhere in internal/ — verified by search. Per fleet MVP acceptance bar, every consequential action must emit a 4903 audit event signed via Signet. Add audit emission on: review publish (kind 1111), signing events, context retrieval from Chartroom. Create an audit publisher in internal/publisher or internal/contextvm.
close_reason: Added kind-4903 audit publisher, audited signer, review and Chartroom retrieval audit emissions

title: Wire context builder to Chartroom /search (replace local Qdrant)
description: Drydock queries its own local Qdrant collections directly via internal/contextbuilder/qdrant_provider.go:21-80 instead of using Chartroom. Per Wave 2 MVP, Drydock must be Chartroom-backed. Replace the QdrantProvider with a ChartRoomProvider that calls Chartroom's /search endpoint with a bearer token. This is the #1 blocker to the MVP acceptance bar — the 'first signed review from Chartroom context' proof cannot be demonstrated until this lands.
close_reason: Implemented Chartroom /search context provider with config wiring and Qdrant dev fallback

title: Fail closed on local signer fallback in production
description: Roadmap remediation: Drydock production/Lemmy no-nsec proof must be Signet/NIP-46 only. Add production validation requiring DRYDOCK_SIGNER_BUNKER_URL and rejecting DRYDOCK_SIGNER_NSEC/NSEC_FILE in production; keep local signer dev-only; update docs/tests. File follow-up for durable 4903 audit outbox if larger than this change.
close_reason: Implemented production fail-closed Signet/NIP-46 signer validation, prevented production nsec fallback, updated tests/docs, and filed DRYDOCK-qux for durable 4903 audit outbox.

title: Fix payment token melt: atomic reservation, rollback, and real reconciliation
description: internal/payment/service.go:215-299, db/store_payments.go:90-112, schema.go:235-237. Token is melted then MarkReviewPaymentTokenSpent; if UpsertSubscription or MarkReviewPaymentAuthorized fails, token is already spent, future calls hit IsTokenHashUsed and permanently deny token_already_used, while AuthorizePatch only treats status==authorized as success. The code comment claims reconciliation exists but there is NO reconciliation implementation. Also IsTokenHashUsed check-then-insert has a replay race before melt. Fix: atomically reserve token hash (unique-constraint insert) BEFORE external mint/invoice calls, distinguish unique-violation replay from DB failure, implement an actual reconciliation path that verifies settlement and retries subscription/authorization, and return a recoverable pending state instead of permanent denial. Category: reliability / money. Depends on invoice settlement verification.
close_reason: Atomic token-hash reservation before mint calls, real reconciliation of melted-but-unauthorized tokens (settle->finalize), payment_pending recoverable state, and subscriptions record invoiced amount; tests added

title: Enforce reviewer/requester authorization on marketplace accept/reject/feedback
description: internal/marketplace/router.go:307-350 (RecordAcceptance/RecordRejection), registry.go:387-435, handler.go:114-249. Handlers overwrite reviewer pubkey from event sender but never verify sender == assignment.ReviewerPubkey, nor that status is currently pending/unexpired. HandleAssignmentIntent stores assignments from arbitrary req.Sender with no authority check (forge payable assignments). Feedback/rating: any pubkey knowing a review event ID can rate, manipulating reputation. Fix: require acceptance.ReviewerPubkey==assignment.ReviewerPubkey, gate state transitions on current status, require assignment intents signed by configured service/router authority or validated against an authorized patch/payment record, restrict feedback to requester/patch author with one-per-assignment. Depends on ingest signature verification. Category: security.
close_reason: Enforced accept/reject reviewer-pubkey + pending/unexpired authorization, assignment-intent authority signing, and requester/author-only one-per-assignment feedback with tests

title: Verify Lightning invoice settlement before authorizing paid access
description: internal/payment/service.go:271-299, nwc.go:198-222. After mint.MeltToken succeeds the service marks token spent and authorizes access/subscription without calling LookupInvoice to confirm the NWC wallet actually received/settled the invoice. A mint/client inconsistency or false paid response grants paid access without confirmed funds. Fix: after melt, call LookupInvoice(invoice.ID) and require Settled==true before MarkReviewPaymentTokenSpent/UpsertSubscription/MarkReviewPaymentAuthorized; persist unresolved melts for reconciliation instead of authorizing. Category: fake-completion / money.
close_reason: fixed: verified NWC lookup_invoice settlement before Cashu payment authorization; unsettled/lookup-failed melts stay recoverable as token_spent without access; added settled/unsettled regression tests; build and full tests pass

title: Verify event ID + signature on live ingest path before dispatch
description: Root cause security hole. internal/listener/listener.go:164 calls processor.ProcessEvent and internal/ingest/processor.go ProcessEvent (lines ~150-265) dispatches events to review queue, conversation, codechat, ContextVM router, IDE gateway (30078) and marketplace (31990/7000) handlers WITHOUT ever calling event.CheckID() or event.VerifySignature(). Only contextvm.Transport.Subscribe verifies signatures, but the production listener path does not use it. Forged/malformed relay events can trigger reviews, mutate marketplace assignment state, invoke ContextVM methods, and drive IDE gateway. Fix: verify CheckID()+VerifySignature() (and reject expired/future timestamps) at the top of ProcessEvent, reject invalid events with a logged metric, add tests with tampered id/sig/pubkey. Category: security.
close_reason: Implemented ingest-boundary Nostr event integrity validation: ProcessEvent now rejects mismatched IDs, invalid signatures, and implausible timestamps before storage/dispatch, increments the rejected-events metric, and logs the rejection reason. Added focused ingest tests for ID mismatch rejection/no dispatch, valid signed dispatch, and future timestamp rejection. Verified with CGO_ENABLED=1 go build ./... and CGO_ENABLED=1 go test ./internal/ingest/... ./internal/listener/... ./...

title: P0: PR author can influence review policy via fork config
description:
In internal/repo/service.go, preparePRTip() claims to read .drydock.yaml from canonical repo, but PR clone and canonical fetch share the same cache key (repoID). If repo was first cloned from fork URL, ReadFileAtDefaultRef() reads fork's origin/HEAD, letting PR authors influence review policy.

**Impact**: Critical - security boundary violation. Malicious PR authors can modify review behavior.

**Fix**: Keep separate cache entry/remote for canonical repository, or fetch config from canonical URLs under distinct local clone.

**Files**: internal/repo/service.go, internal/repo/manager.go
close_reason: Fixed: canonical repo config is now read from a distinct canonical cache path for PR tips and patch series, preventing fork-populated caches from influencing review policy. Added regression coverage and verified go test ./... passes.

title: P0: Payment gating implemented but never wired into runtime
description:
Payment gating is fully implemented in internal/payment/service.go but never used:
- main.go never constructs a payment.Service
- runner.process() never calls AuthorizePatch()
- Repo payment policy is completely unenforced
- Every patch can be reviewed without payment checks

**Impact**: Critical - payment-based access control is completely bypassed.

**Fix**: Instantiate payment service in main.go, load repo payment policy in runner, gate review execution before expensive operations.

**Files**: cmd/drydock/main.go, internal/pipeline/runner.go, internal/payment/service.go
close_reason: Wired payment authorization into runtime/pipeline, applied per-endpoint LLM API keys, made embedding dimension configurable, and registered subscribed event handlers.

title: P0: Publisher marks reviews as published before relay confirmation
description:
PublishReview() in internal/publisher/service.go writes review_event_id to review_log BEFORE publishing to relays. The retry/idempotency check treats any existing review_event_id as proof publication succeeded. If relay publish fails after SetReviewEventID(), next retry will skip publication and mark review as published anyway.

**Impact**: Critical - reviews marked published may never reach relays, causing silent data loss.

**Fix**: Separate signed event id from published state. Only short-circuit retries when review_log.status=published. Clear provisional ID on publish failure.

**Files**: internal/publisher/service.go, internal/db/store.go
close_reason: Fixed: Added GetReviewEventIDAndStatus and ClearReviewEventID methods. Publisher now checks status=published before skipping and clears provisional event ID on publish failure.

title: P0: SQLite driver mismatch in config validation
description:
Config validation in internal/config/config.go uses 'sqlite3' driver while runtime in internal/db/store.go uses 'sqlite' (modernc.org/sqlite). This causes startup validation to fail incorrectly, potentially bricking service startup.

**Impact**: Critical - prevents service startup in some configurations.

**Fix**: Either validate through the same path the service uses (db.Open/Store.Ping), or switch to 'sqlite' driver name in validation code.

**Files**: internal/config/config.go, internal/db/store.go
close_reason: Fixed: Changed driver from sqlite3 to sqlite in config validation, added modernc.org/sqlite import

title: eval: the security and Nostr harnesses score a mock scripted from the answer key
description:
Code: S2 (confidence). Files: eval/security_harness_test.go:123-198, eval/nostr_harness_test.go:88-107, :35-45.
Evidence: reviewerCandidates synthesizes the 'model's' findings DIRECTLY from the expected labels (security_harness_test.go:126-132 ranges over expected and copies File/Line), marshals them as the canned FakeLLM reply, then scores them against those same labels. verifiedCandidates:172-182 scripts the verifier's answer per candidate with matchesAny(expected, candidate) — the mock is TOLD which candidates are true positives and refutes exactly the rest. The suite then asserts 'securityverify cut the false-positive rate', 'improved precision', 'did not drop recall' (:58-72). Also withVerify.Latency > prLensCIBudget (:73) times two in-memory fakes.
Worse: eval/nostr_harness_test.go calls the same two helpers, so the entire NP25 rule eval (9 rules x vulnerable/fixed fixtures with per-rule line numbers) NEVER EXECUTES A LINE of nostrscan — grep for securityscan./PresenceRules/AnalyzeAbsences in eval/ matches only nostrscan.Detect.
Correct shape: the fixtures are real and already paired vulnerable/fixed — run them through the production path auditengine/engine.go:322-335 uses: securityscan.NewWithRuleSets(nostrscan.PresenceRulesForRoles(roles), nostrscan.SurfaceRules()).ScanFiles(...) plus nostrscan.AnalyzeAbsences(...), and score THOSE findings. If the intent is only to test verifier wiring, delete the precision/recall/FPR/latency assertions.
Cost: the repo's only end-to-end quality gate for the Nostr lens and for securityverify is a closed loop over its own answer key. Every NP25 rule could be deleted and this suite stays green.

title: lsp-bridge image runs as root and pins nothing
description:
Code: I1 (structural, security surface + drift). File: docker/lsp-bridge/Dockerfile.
Evidence: (a) no USER directive anywhere (grep -c '^USER' = 0) — lsp-bridge and every language server it spawns run as root; gopls installs to /root/go/bin (:34). The sibling Dockerfile:32-35 does this correctly with adduser -D -u 1000 drydock + USER drydock. (b) :44 pipes a remote script to a root shell (curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_20.x | bash -). (c) Unpinned: gopls@latest (:35), pip3 install python-lsp-server (:41), npm install -g typescript typescript-language-server (:46), rust-analyzer releases/latest/download (:56). (d) builder is golang:1.26-alpine (:11) but the runtime separately downloads go1.23.6 (:33) to build gopls — go.mod declares go 1.26, so gopls is built by a toolchain three minor versions behind the module it must parse. (e) line 1 contains two UTF-8 REPLACEMENT CHARACTERs (bytes ef bf bd ef bf bd) where an em-dash belongs.
Failure: the bridge executes third-party language servers against attacker-supplied repository contents (manager.go:162-163 sets cmd.Dir = repoPath); gopls/rust-analyzer honour in-repo config, so any escape runs as uid 0 with drydock_data mounted (docker-compose.yml:99).
Correct shape: mirror Dockerfile:30-35 (non-root user + USER); COPY --from=builder /usr/local/go /usr/local/go instead of re-downloading; pin each server version the way Dockerfile:7 already pins BETTERLEAKS_VERSION=v1.7.4.
Cost: security surface, plus two builds of the same commit produce different images.

title: ratelimit: Cleanup is never called, so the rate_limits table grows without bound
description:
Code: S5 (structural, resource lifecycle). File: internal/ratelimit/limiter.go:174-178.
Evidence: Cleanup deletes rows older than 2x Window; its doc comment says 'Should be called periodically (e.g., every hour).' It has ZERO callers in the repo (only the definition and the CleanupOldRateLimits impls). main.go runs four other background tickers — prompt refine 5m (:967), Cashu reconcile 1m (:1010), requeue sweep 10m (:1042), marketplace expiry (:1082) — and none calls it.
Correct shape: one line in the existing 10-minute sweep goroutine at main.go:1042-1077 iterating the three constructed limiters.
Cost: every Allow() inserts a row and nothing ever deletes one; GetRateLimitCount/CheckAndIncrementRateLimit scan the table on every rate-limited request. Unbounded SQLite growth with a comment that makes it look handled.
Kludge stands in for: wiring an existing method into an existing ticker (exists: yes).
close_reason: Fixed: cmd/drydock/main.go now runs an hourly goroutine calling Cleanup on all three limiters (codechat, review-order, marketplace-feedback). Placed at limiter construction rather than inside the 10-minute sweep, because that sweep is guarded by 'if pipelineRunner != nil' while the limiters are always constructed.

title: LSP bridge client is built without an auth token, so the capability is silently dead in the shipped compose profile
description:
Code: S9/S5 (structural, false confidence). Files: cmd/drydock/main.go:432, internal/config/config.go:120 & :268, internal/lspbridge/client.go:22-27.
Evidence: main.go builds lspbridge.NewClient(cfg.LSPBridgeURL) — token-less. config.Config has LSPBridgeURL but NO token field at all. docker-compose.yml:97 hard-requires LSP_BRIDGE_AUTH_TOKEN (:? form). server/handler.go:438-451 authorized() returns true only when zero tokens are configured — otherwise /analyze 401s. NewClientWithToken exists and is called ONLY from client_test.go:58.
Failure: 'docker compose --profile lsp up' -> main.go:433 pings /healthz which is NOT auth-gated (handler.go:78-85) -> 200 -> main.go:438 logs 'LSP bridge connected' and registers WithLSPBridge -> every Analyze returns 'lspbridge: HTTP 401' -> the LSP context layer silently degrades to git-grep. Logs and /readyz both report healthy. /healthz even returns AuthRequired:true and the client never reads it.
Correct shape: add LSPBridgeToken: envOrDefault("DRYDOCK_LSP_BRIDGE_TOKEN", "") beside LSPBridgeURL and call the existing lspbridge.NewClientWithToken.
Cost: false confidence — the flagship deployment path advertises a capability it can never use.
close_reason: Fixed: added Config.LSPBridgeToken (DRYDOCK_LSP_BRIDGE_TOKEN, falling back to LSP_BRIDGE_AUTH_TOKEN) and switched main.go to the existing lspbridge.NewClientWithToken. Also wired DRYDOCK_LSP_BRIDGE_TOKEN into the drydock-core service in docker-compose.yml (previously the token reached only the bridge service) and documented LSP_BRIDGE_AUTH_TOKEN in .env.example beside DRYDOCK_SIGNER_BUNKER_URL.

title: Two copies of security-critical repo-relative path confinement
description:
Code: S4 (structural, security). Files: internal/contextbuilder/safe_files.go:14-65 vs internal/workspacesnapshot/snapshot.go:803-824, 986-1003.
Evidence: normalizeRepositoryRelativePath and normalizePath are line-for-line the same — identical hand-rolled windowsAbsolute drive-letter check, identical NUL check, identical .. component loop, identical Clean + ../ and / prefix checks. secureRepositoryPath's per-component os.Lstat symlink loop is a copy of rejectSymlinkComponents. Only the error sentinel and an allowDot flag differ.
Correct shape: one internal/safepath with Normalize(path string, allowDot bool) and RejectSymlinkComponents(root, target); both packages call it. No cycle: workspacesnapshot imports no internal packages and contextbuilder does not import it.
Cost: security surface — a hardening fix (UNC paths, NFD unicode, case-insensitive FS) applied to one copy silently leaves the other exploitable, and nothing in the build links them.

title: securityscan: hand-rolled unified-diff parser where go-gitdiff is already a direct dependency
description:
Code: S4/S8 (structural). Files: internal/securityscan/scanner.go:239-307 (ParseDiffAddedLines, parseHunkNewStart), internal/securityscan/provider.go:72-85 (extractChangedFiles).
Evidence: a hand-rolled diff parser down to a manual digit-accumulation loop (:294-300), plus a third pass over '+++ b/'. github.com/bluekeyes/go-gitdiff v0.7.1 is a DIRECT dependency (go.mod:11) already used for exactly this in internal/contextbuilder/providers.go:51-57 (parsePatch). Concrete failures: (1) the '\ No newline at end of file' marker hits none of the +, -, +++, ---, @@ branches, falls into the context branch (:275-279) and increments newLineNum, so every subsequent added line in that file is attributed one line too high; (2) 'git diff --no-prefix' / diff.noprefix output has no b/ prefix, so currentFile is never set and the whole diff scans as empty, skipping every file silently (scanner.go:88-92).
Also: agenticreview/discovery.go designates contextbuilder.NewPatchFacade().Analyze as the AUTHORITATIVE patch analysis and rejects snapshots whose patch does not match the filtered diff — securityscan feeds the same pipeline with a second, disagreeing parse.
Correct shape: gitdiff.Parse -> file.TextFragments -> fragment.NewPosition + Lines[].Op == gitdiff.OpAdd; extractChangedFiles becomes file.NewName. Deletes ~70 lines.
Cost: silent line-number drift and silent whole-file skips in the path that decides which secrets and SAST hits get reported.

title: Replace six forked git-exec helpers with one hardened shared helper
description:
Code: S4 (structural). Files: internal/repo/manager.go:729 runGit (+ :745, :767, :813 variants), internal/codemap/builder.go:318 gitOutput / :327 gitBlob / :178 listTree, internal/nostrscan/detector.go:617 gitOutput / :266 gitBlob / :218 gitFiles, internal/contextbuilder/providers.go:619 runGit, internal/auditengine/engine.go:886 gitOutput, internal/workspacesnapshot/snapshot.go:1122 runGitBytes.
Evidence: six package-local wrappers around exec.CommandContext("git","-C",repo,...). Only workspacesnapshot.runGitBytes sets GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 and extracts ExitError.Stderr (verified: the only GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT in the repo). The other five inherit ambient env and can block on a credential prompt inside a review pipeline worker. Error shapes diverge three ways, so callers cannot match uniformly. contextbuilder.runGit additionally discards CombinedOutput in its error, which is why analyzeHistoryContent:509 forked it again inline.
Correct shape: lift workspacesnapshot.runGitBytes into internal/gitexec (Run, RunBytes, Blob, ListTree) and point the five other forks at it. repo.Manager's limit-streaming variants stay but build on the shared env/error base.
Cost: a hang class exists in five of six forks that the sixth already solved; every new git call site re-forks the wrapper.

title: repo: three copies of git-apply stdin boilerplate, two discard the write error
description:
Code: S4 (structural). File: internal/repo/manager.go:687-725 applySinglePatch, :1207-1229 checkPatchApplies, :1232-1254 applyPatchContent.
Evidence: three functions repeat timeout ctx -> exec.CommandContext(git,-C,path,apply,...,-) -> StdinPipe -> goroutine io.WriteString -> CombinedOutput -> wrap, differing only in flags (--3way --index / --check / --index). applySinglePatch propagates the write error via errCh and checks 'writeErr != nil && writeErr != io.ErrClosedPipe' at :721. The copies at :1222 and :1247 leave io.WriteString's return value completely unassigned.
Failure: a failed/short pipe write to 'git apply --check' makes git see a truncated patch and exit non-zero; checkPatchApplies returns an error and buildAutoFixPatch:1127 logs 'suggestion does not apply cleanly' at Debug and silently skips a valid fix — indistinguishable from a genuinely non-applying patch.
Correct shape: one (m *Manager) runGitApply(ctx, repoPath, patch string, flags ...string) error holding applySinglePatch's already-correct stdin handling; three callers pass flags.
Cost: hardening drift — one copy was fixed, the two copy-pasted siblings were not.

title: marketplace: acceptance/rejection handlers forge a mutated event instead of calling the typed path
description:
Code: S4 (structural). File: internal/marketplace/handler.go:258-272, 296-311.
Evidence: handleContextVMAcceptance/handleContextVMRejection decode params with ParamsAs[ReviewAcceptance], throw the result away, then forge 'event := req.Event; event.Content = string(req.Msg.Params); event.PubKey = req.Sender' and pass it to router.HandleAcceptance, which unmarshals the same JSON a second time. The forged event's ID no longer matches its mutated Content.
Correct shape: the pattern one function away at handler.go:290 — router.complete(ctx, completion, req.Sender.Hex(), req.Event.ID.Hex()) (router.go:394). Add sibling recordAcceptance/recordRejection with the same signature.
Cost: double decode, and a live landmine — the forged event fails CheckID(), so adding signature verification inside HandleAcceptance (as HandleCompletion at router.go:383 already does) would reject every legitimate acceptance. That asymmetry already forced handleContextVMCompletion to verify on req.Event BEFORE delegating.
Kludge stands in for: router.complete's typed signature (exists: yes, router.go:394).

title: db: double-spend detection by driver error-message substring, spelled two different ways
description:
Code: S5 (confidence, security/money path). Files: internal/db/store_payments.go:1049-1055, internal/db/store.go:2950.
Evidence: isSQLiteUniqueConstraint does strings.Contains(msg, "UNIQUE constraint failed") || strings.Contains(msg, "constraint failed: UNIQUE"); store.go:2950 in the same package uses a narrower strings.Contains(err.Error(), "UNIQUE constraint"). The helper gates ErrTokenHashAlreadyReserved (:103, :137) — the replay/race denial on Cashu token reservation.
Correct shape: 'var e *sqlite.Error; errors.As(err, &e) && e.Code() == sqlite3.SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_UNIQUE'. modernc.org/sqlite v1.39.1 (go.mod:18) exports type Error with Code() int. Then delete store.go:2950's copy and call the one helper.
Cost: a driver message reformat turns a double-spend replay into a generic DB error and the caller stops distinguishing 'already reserved' from 'database down'. The two predicates already disagree today.
Kludge stands in for: the driver's typed constraint code (exists: yes, modernc.org/sqlite).
close_reason: Fixed: isSQLiteUniqueConstraint now uses errors.As(*sqlite.Error) + Code() against SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_UNIQUE (2067) and SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_PRIMARYKEY (1555), replacing the message-substring match; store.go:2930's separate narrower substring predicate now calls the same helper. Codes verified empirically against modernc.org/sqlite v1.39.1. Added TestIsSQLiteUniqueConstraintUsesDriverCode covering unique, primary-key, wrapped, NOT-NULL (must not match) and look-alike-message (must not match) cases.

title: db: money path uses err == sql.ErrNoRows and 79 bare unwrapped driver errors
description:
Code: S4/S5 (structural, money path). Files: internal/db/store_payments.go, store_marketplace.go, store_codechat.go, store.go, internal/reviewsession/store.go.

title: repo: commitSnapshot discards the git status error and treats failure as 'tree clean'
description:
Code: S5 (structural, publishes wrong artifact). File: internal/repo/manager.go:1192.
Evidence: 'status, _ := m.runGit(ctx, repoPath, "status", "--porcelain")' — error discarded, then empty string is read as 'already clean' and commitSnapshot returns nil without committing. Every other runGit call in the same function checks (:1188, :1197).
Failure: git status fails (index.lock contention from concurrent worktree ops in the same Manager, or a corrupt index) -> status=="" -> no snapshot commit -> buildAutoFixPatch applies suggestions and runs 'git diff --cached HEAD' at :1162 against the PRE-patch HEAD -> the published autofix patch contains the entire reviewed PR diff plus the fixes. Wired live via pipeline/runner.go:1144.
Correct shape: check the error as the sibling calls do; better, use 'git diff --cached --quiet HEAD' and branch on exit code instead of scraping stdout for emptiness.
Cost: silent wrong-output path in a user-facing published artifact.
close_reason: Fixed: commitSnapshot now checks the 'git status --porcelain' error instead of discarding it, so a status failure returns an error rather than being read as 'tree already clean'. Removes the path where the published autofix patch could contain the entire reviewed PR diff.

title: securityverify: LLM JSON parsed without fence stripping, unlike every other structured call

Cost: a fenced response makes every verifier vote verdictIndeterminate. At :202 it degrades to 'verification unavailable'; at :273 it aborts classify and kills the whole security result. Untested.

title: Meta-review fails 100% of runs: unbounded prompt overflow + brittle JSON parsing + invisible async failures
description: Root cause #6 in docs/investigations/review-mismatch-2026-08-12.md. Meta-review triggered 50 times in 2 weeks with 0 successes: 17 context overflows (up to 12.3M tokens vs 262k limit) because metaReviewUserPrompt embeds the full unbounded PatchDiff + bundle (internal/metareview/service.go:328-347); 31 strict-JSON schema rejections (e.g. reasoning_quality as string); 2 circuit-breaker. Failures are async and invisible (internal/pipeline/runner.go:681-694), leaving meta_review_log empty. Fix: cap/summarize the diff and bundle to a token budget; tolerant JSON repair (coerce string numbers etc.) before rejection; persist failed attempts to an audit table with reason; expose failure metrics; make the 'frontier' endpoint an explicit config (default local llama-3.3-70b is not frontier — document/allow real frontier via config).
acceptance_criteria: Meta-review succeeds on real-size PR diffs in a test; failed attempts recorded in audit table; metrics counter for failures
close_reason: Bound meta-review diff/context inputs, added tolerant output parsing, durable attempt audits, failure metrics, and configurable frontier endpoint guidance.

title: Shared mutable checkout races across concurrent reviews of same repo
description: Root cause #3 in docs/investigations/review-mismatch-2026-08-12.md. All reviews for a repo_id share one checkout (internal/repo/manager.go:427-441) with in-memory mutexes held only per git operation (manager.go:24-29,210-233,500-503); the rest of the review (context building, LLM calls, scanning, autofix, cleanup) reads the working tree unlocked (internal/pipeline/runner.go:400-446,500-619; internal/contextbuilder/providers.go:78-112). In the 2-week corpus, 87/324 successfully prepared reviews overlapped another same-repo review. Fix: per-review git worktrees (git worktree add) held for the full review lifetime, or a repo lock held from prepare through cleanup; add checkout identity assertions (expected tip) before context building and scans.
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent same-repo reviews operate on isolated trees; integration test for two overlapping reviews of one repo
close_reason: Eliminated shared review checkouts with canonical-linked per-review worktrees, full-lifetime cleanup/pinning, checkout identity assertions, and concurrent same-repo coverage.

title: PR reviews diff against stale origin/HEAD, producing wrong-base mega-diffs
description: Root cause #2 in docs/investigations/review-mismatch-2026-08-12.md. DiffAgainstDefaultBranch (internal/repo/manager.go:235-274) diffs the PR tip against the cached canonical clone's origin/HEAD with no event-asserted base; stale bases produced 1,709-4,608-file / 21-42MB diffs for 1-17-file PRs. All 300/300 sampled mismatched file references in the corpus came from these stale-base diffs. Fallback to fork clone (internal/repo/service.go:178-187) lets a fork-controlled origin/HEAD choose the base. Fix: require a provenance-checked base commit/ref for kind 1618/1619 events (use event-asserted base when present; verify merge-base plausibility), persist and publish base/tip/diff sha256, and reject implausibly large file/byte deltas instead of silently truncating.
acceptance_criteria: PR prepare records base+tip+diff hashes; oversized deltas fail closed with clear reason; unit test covering stale canonical clone
close_reason: Added verified event-asserted/implicit PR bases, bounded fail-closed diff limits, persisted and published base/tip/diff provenance, and stale-canonical/fallback coverage.

title: git.sharegap.net rejects pushes >1MB (HTTP 413) — Gitea mirror frozen at a213791
description: The GRASP relay (nostr:// origin) accepts pushes and is current at b092b21, but the Gitea mirror cascadia/drydock (web UI + plain git clones) is stuck at a213791 — the last commit before ef5aeec, which added assets/drydock-icon.png + assets/drydock-banner.png (~1.25MB). CORRECTION after code inspection: the route is NOT broken/mismatched. processor.go:217 routes kinds 31650,1651,1653 to ideGateway.HandleEvent; listener subscribes to them; extension.ts uses the same constants. The real issue is that the whole IDE stack still uses kinds CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md mark DEPRECATED (31650 session; 1651-1654 review/fix req+resp). Target migration per project convention: IDE session state 31650 -> 30078; IDE review/fix request+response 1651-1654 -> ContextVM kind 25910 JSON-RPC methods (the sanctioned 'ContextVM commands' scheme). Files that must change in lockstep: internal/idegateway/types.go (+handler.go kind switch/response kinds/method dispatch), internal/ingest/processor.go (routing case), internal/listener/listener.go (subscribedKinds + TestSubscribedKindsSet), extensions/vscode-drydock/src/extension.ts (publish/subscribe kinds), docs/ide-integration.md. docs/event-kinds.md no longer exists.

title: P1: Payment token melted before authorization finalized
description:
In processTokenPayment(), token is melted before authorization state is durably finalized. If UpsertSubscription() or MarkReviewPaymentAuthorized() fails after MeltToken() succeeds, user loses funds without access granted, and retry path has no reconciliation state.

**Fix**: Make post-melt state transition recoverable/transactional - persist settled/spent state first, then authorize in one durable step.

**Files**: internal/payment/service.go
close_reason: Fixed payment token timing issue. Token is now marked as 'token_spent' immediately after melting, creating a recoverable state before authorization. If subscription creation or authorization fails, the token_spent status prevents fund loss and enables reconciliation. Updated schema, added MarkReviewPaymentTokenSpent method, updated IsTokenHashUsed to prevent double-spending during recovery window. All tests pass.

title: P1: Vector dimension hardcoded to 768
description:
Vector dimension is hardcoded to 768 when creating Qdrant collections. If DRYDOCK_EMBED_MODEL is changed to model with different embedding size, startup looks healthy but indexing/search fails at runtime.

**Fix**: Make dimension configurable, or probe embedder once at startup and derive collection size from returned vector length.

**Files**: cmd/drydock/main.go, internal/codeindex/indexer.go
close_reason: Wired payment authorization into runtime/pipeline, applied per-endpoint LLM API keys, made embedding dimension configurable, and registered subscribed event handlers.

title: P1: Listener high-water-mark resume logic is inverted
description:
In internal/listener/listener.go, persisted high-water-mark resume logic:
  if hwmWithOverlap < since { since = hwmWithOverlap }
This chooses EARLIER timestamp instead of resuming near last processed event, so restarts replay default lookback window instead of using persisted watermark.

**Fix**: Set since to persisted watermark minus overlap (bounded at zero), choosing newer of two cursors.

**Files**: internal/listener/listener.go
close_reason: Fixed: Changed comparison from < to > so listener uses the more recent timestamp (hwm vs lookback) instead of always using the older one

title: P1: Shared symbols.Extractor risks concurrency issues
description:
DefaultProviders() in internal/contextbuilder/providers.go creates one shared symbols.Extractor reused across builds. Tree-sitter extractors are mutable and not safe to share (codeindex/indexer.go creates them per call). With multiple pipeline workers, this can produce racy/corrupted symbol extraction.

**Fix**: Create extractor per Build() invocation or pool behind synchronization.

**Files**: internal/contextbuilder/providers.go, internal/symbols/extractor.go
close_reason: Fixed by creating extractor per Build() call instead of sharing one. Tree-sitter parsers are mutable and now thread-safe. All tests pass.

title: P1: Event handlers not registered for subscribed kinds
description:
Listener subscribes to DM, IDE, and marketplace kinds, but main.go never registers CodeChatHandler, IDEGatewayHandler, or MarketplaceHandler. Events are marked ingested then dropped silently, making integrations look live when not.

**Fix**: Either wire handlers before subscribing or remove unhandled kinds from subscribedKinds and emit startup warning.

**Files**: cmd/drydock/main.go, internal/listener/listener.go
close_reason: Wired payment authorization into runtime/pipeline, applied per-endpoint LLM API keys, made embedding dimension configurable, and registered subscribed event handlers.

title: P1: Rate limiter race condition - check and increment not atomic
description:
Allow() in internal/ratelimit/limiter.go does separate Check() and IncrementRateLimit() with no transactional reservation. Under concurrency, multiple requests can observe same capacity and exceed configured limit.

**Fix**: Add single store method that checks-and-increments atomically in one transaction.

**Files**: internal/ratelimit/limiter.go, internal/db/store.go
close_reason: Fixed race condition by implementing atomic check-and-increment in Store interface. Added CheckAndIncrementRateLimit() method that uses SQL transactions (SQLStore) and mutex locking (MemoryStore) to prevent concurrent requests from exceeding rate limit. Added concurrency test to verify fix. All tests pass.

title: Severity vocabulary is untyped magic strings across five finding subsystems
description:
Code: S4 (drift). title: contextbuilder exposes two public APIs for every deterministic layer, and a test asserts f(x)==f(x)

title: nostrscan: *UseNameRE regexes overmatch because their discriminating suffix is optional
description:
Code: S8 (confidence). File: internal/nostrscan/absence.go:77-81.
Evidence: the five *UseNameRE are applied to node.symbol.Name — a single identifier already extracted by tree-sitter. Four end in an OPTIONAL group, e.g. (?i)(?:store|save|persist|render|display|trust|accept|process)[A-Za-z0-9_]*(?:event|message|profile|contact|dm)? — because (?:...)? is optional and the pattern is unanchored, the trailing group contributes nothing and the rule is exactly 'name contains one of these verbs'. So displayName, processRequest and acceptHeader all set v2Use (-> NOSTR-V2, high); v7UseNameRE's bare get/cache/find matches budgetCheck and widgetStore (-> NOSTR-V7, CRITICAL, if any event.id text appears in the body). Only v1UseNameRE (:79) has required suffixes.
Correct shape: these are substring checks over a word list — slices.ContainsFunc(useVerbs, func(v string) bool { return strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(name), v) }) with the verb lists as named var slices. If the suffixes ARE meant to be required, anchor them and drop the '?'.
Cost: the regex form advertises precision it does not have; these feed critical/high findings at 0.79 confidence into the reviewer prompt.
NOTE: the rest of the regex corpus in securityscan/rules.go and absence.go is explicitly CLEARED — internal/symbols is declarations-only (no call-site or expression API, zero tree-sitter query usage in the repo), so an AST replacement does not exist and would be bigger than what is there.

title: reviewsession: randomized BFS over map[string]any to find a field whose JSON path is fixed
description:
Code: S5 (confidence). File: internal/reviewsession/compaction.go:121-149 (+ store_test.go:65,108,139,173,175).
Evidence: findSummaryAndFindings breadth-first-searches an arbitrary map[string]any for keys summary|Summary|findings|Findings at any depth. RunOutput has no json tags so the key is 'Review'; ReviewerOutput has json:"summary"/json:"findings". The path is fixed: .Review.summary / .Review.findings. Cost: any sibling struct gaining a Go field named Summary or Findings marshals to a colliding key and starts winning the BFS race at random, silently substituting the planner's or walkthrough's summary into continuation history — unfalsifiable at runtime.

title: agenticreview: the agent tool loop is implemented twice in one package
description:
Code: S4 (drift). Files: internal/agenticreview/loop.go:110-192 vs internal/agenticreview/reviewer.go:680-781.
Evidence: two copies of preflight token count -> MaxModelContext check -> cumulative check -> Complete -> turn++ -> cancellation-vs-transport classification -> Usage.TotalTokens<=0 manual accounting over content+tool names+arguments -> append message -> per-tool-call MaxToolCalls check -> Dispatch -> json.Marshal(toolResult) -> terminal-tool detection. Only the terminal tool (selection.finalize vs review.submit), the evidence ledger, the empty-assistant nudge and servedModel differ. Already drifted: reviewer.go:706-707 populates Message.PromptTokens/CompletionTokens for persistence and loop.go does not; reviewer.go nudges on an empty assistant turn while loop.go:152 appends the tool-less message and burns the remaining turn budget re-sending an identical request.
Correct shape: extend LoopRequest with TerminalTool string, an OnAssistant func(CompletionMessage) bool hook (nudge + servedModel) and an OnToolResult func(ToolCall, agenttools.Result) hook (EvidenceLedger.Record + transcript sink); have ExecuteReviewer call LoopRunner.Run and map LoopTrace -> ReviewerTrace via the existing reviewerTrace() at reviewer.go:784.
Cost: ~100 lines of budget-enforcement and cancellation logic that must be fixed twice.

title: metareview hand-rolls a parallel tolerant-JSON stack instead of reusing reviewengine's
description:
Code: S4 (drift). Files: internal/metareview/types.go:147-254 and :308-440 vs internal/reviewengine/structured.go:32-123; internal/metareview/service.go:238-245.
Evidence: two fully independent tolerant-parse stacks sharing zero code. reviewengine re-prompts the model with a schema hint (2 bounded repair attempts). metareview repairs the bytes locally: repairInvalidJSONEscapes (:238-254) rewrites invalid \\x escapes, then a bank of six coercion helpers — flexibleItems, parseFlexibleString/Float/Int/Bool/Strings (:308-440) — that accept scalar-for-array, string-for-number, 'yes'-for-bool. metareview/service.go:238-245 is also the ONLY LLM call in the slice that does not set JSONMode. The inverse correlation is the tell. Additionally types.go:219-236 extractMetaReviewJSON is a second implementation of llmutil.ExtractJSON (equivalent today, structurally divergent: LastIndex-based fence close vs line-based).
Correct shape: set JSONMode:true on service.go:243, replace extractMetaReviewJSON with llmutil.ExtractJSON, and route the call through reviewengine.completeStructuredWithParser (already generic over T) with ParseMetaReviewOutput as the parser. Delete types.go:219-254 and the parseFlexible* bank.
Cost: ~250 lines of untestable coercion that silently accepts '0.7', 'yes' and scalar-for-array, so a model producing wrong-typed output is graded as if it complied; llmutil currently has exactly one importer, so the next fence-format fix lands in one place only.

title: Three incompatible definitions of 'the same finding' in the dedupe path
description:
Code: S4 (drift). Files: internal/reviewengine/ensemble.go:250-253 (findingKey, used by mergeFindings:264), internal/reviewengine/ensemble.go:366-424 (DeduplicateFindings), internal/securityscan/dedup.go:12-106 (DeduplicateFindings).
Evidence: (1) file:(line/5)*5:category — a 5-line QUANTISED BUCKET; (2) same file+category with a +/-2-line SLIDING WINDOW; (3) same file+category with a +/-3-line window and a [Line-3,EndLine+3] span for sensitive findings. The bucket at ensemble.go:251 has the classic boundary defect: lines 4 and 5 land in different buckets and never merge, while lines 0 and 4 do. Both bucket and window live in ensemble.go 115 lines apart and both claim to dedupe findings. pipeline/runner.go:810 calls securityscan.DeduplicateFindings while securityreview/stage.go:154 calls reviewengine.DeduplicateFindings — two same-named exported functions with different arities and windows in the same call chain.
Correct shape: delete findingKey and have mergeFindings cluster via the existing window at ensemble.go:366, tracking contributing routes in the representative; have securityscan.DeduplicateFindings delegate to reviewengine.DeduplicateFindings after converting, keeping only the sensitive-span override. Separately rename securityscan.DeduplicateFindings -> MergeScannerFindings, which is what its own doc comment describes.
Cost: a finding's dedupe semantics depend on which path reached it, so the same model output produces different published review contents.

title: idegateway and revieworder map the same service errors to different ContextVM codes
description:
Code: S4 (drift). Files: internal/idegateway/handler.go:429-444 vs internal/revieworder/handler.go:194-215.
Evidence: both call revieworder.SubmitOnDemand and both map its errors. revieworder.reviewOrderRPCError maps ErrRateLimited -> ErrorRateLimited(-32005) and *PaymentDeniedError -> ErrorPaymentRequired(-32006) with a JSON data payload. idegateway maps ErrPaymentDenied -> ErrorUnauthorized(-32001) and has NO ErrRateLimited case, so it falls through to ErrorInternal(-32603). Both are reachable: service.go:265 returns ErrRateLimited; service.go:315/327/334 return *PaymentDeniedError.
Correct shape: export revieworder.reviewOrderRPCError as revieworder.RPCError(err) *contextvm.Error and call it from idegateway.processPatchReviewRequest. One mapping for one error set.
Cost: identical service rejections surface as different protocol codes depending on which door the client knocked on. An IDE client sees -32603 Internal for a rate limit (retryable) and -32001 Unauthorized for payment-required (payable), losing the retryable/reason payload entirely.

title: Four ContextVM envelope validators with four different replay-protection policies
description:
Code: S4/S1 (drift, security). Files: internal/revieworder/handler.go:135-186, internal/marketplace/handler.go:420-448, internal/idegateway/handler.go:839-853, internal/ingest/processor.go:449-459.
Evidence: revieworder.validateEnvelope requires p-tag addressing the service, exactly one method tag, exactly one e tag matching target, and a MANDATORY expiration <= 15min. marketplace.validateMarketplaceFeedbackEnvelope does the same method/e checks but expiration is OPTIONAL and there is NO p-tag check. idegateway.validateRequestEnvelope checks p + session + request tags but has NO method tag and NO expiration. Meanwhile ingest.Processor.handleContextVM already does the p-tag and method-tag check centrally BEFORE dispatch. Each ships its own lifetime constant (maxOrderLifetime, feedbackNotificationMaxLifetime, both 15*time.Minute).
Correct shape: one contextvm.ValidateEnvelope(req Request, method string, relatedID string, opts EnvelopePolicy) *Error in the package all three already import, with ExpirationRequired bool. Delete the per-handler p/method re-checks handleContextVM has already performed; keep only the genuinely per-method bits (related-id binding, session/request binding).
Cost: three handlers on one transport disagree on whether replay protection is mandatory — feedback notifications accept an unexpiring envelope, IDE requests have no expiry check at all. The duplicated central checks make the real one look optional.

title: Signer and RelayPublisher each declared in seven packages, all bound to the same two objects
description:
Code: S4/S7 (drift). Files: internal/publisher/service.go:22,27; conversation/handler.go:34,40; codechat/handler.go:46,54; idegateway/handler.go:42,48; marketplace/router.go:21,27; profile/service.go:39,44; contextvm/transport.go:17. Same pattern: MonitoringRegistry + PaymentAuthorizer byte-identical in pipeline/runner.go:74,79 and revieworder/service.go:52,62; LLMClient in reviewengine/client.go:21 (canonical), metareview/service.go:37, promptrefine/service.go:26 — and the two duplicates already import reviewengine to name reviewengine.ChatRequest/ChatResult inside their own copy; ToolRunner in auditengine/engine.go:110 and nostrprobe/binary.go:15.
Evidence: the composition root (cmd/drydock/main.go:200-620) binds every one to the same internal/signing signer and publisher.NewNostrRelayPublisher(pool, logger). pipeline.Runner and revieworder.Service are both wired to the same monitoring registry and payment service, so the two identical interfaces describe the same object to two consumers.
Correct shape: declare Signer once in internal/signing and RelayPublisher once in internal/publisher (both already imported by all seven consumers); import, do not re-declare. For the pipeline/revieworder pair declare payment.Authorizer and monitoring.Membership in the consumed package. Consumer-side interface idiom argues for one declaration at one consumer, not seven at seven.
Cost: adding a method to signing (e.g. NIP-46 delegation) requires touching seven files; the copies have already diverged in doc comments and in codechat's Keyer shape.

title: contextvm: four identical one-method interfaces and four identical forwarders
description:
Code: S7 (drift). File: internal/contextvm/methods.go:1-53 (whole file).
Evidence: IDEGateway, SecurityAuditor, ReviewOrderer, Marketplace — three are character-for-character identical (RegisterContextVMMethods(router *Router) error) and the fourth differs only in method name (RegisterContextVMHandlers). Then four identical forwarders, each 'if x == nil { return nil }; return x.Register...(router)'. Each has exactly one production implementation, all wired at cmd/drydock/main.go:737-757.
Correct shape: one 'type MethodProvider interface { RegisterContextVMMethods(*Router) error }' plus 'func RegisterMethods(r *Router, providers ...MethodProvider) error'; rename idegateway.Handler.RegisterContextVMHandlers -> RegisterContextVMMethods. The file collapses to ~10 lines and main.go:737-757 becomes one call.
Cost: 53 lines of indirection adding no policy; registering a fifth handler requires editing this file for ceremony alone.
close_reason: Fixed: contextvm/methods.go collapsed from 4 identical interfaces + 4 identical forwarders (53 lines) to one MethodProvider interface + one variadic RegisterMethods (21 lines). idegateway.Handler.RegisterContextVMHandlers renamed to RegisterContextVMMethods. main.go's four registration blocks became one call. Also fixed a latent typed-nil trap the old per-call 'if x == nil' never caught: securityAuditHandler is a *SecurityAuditHandler that may be nil, and RegisterContextVMMethods has no nil-receiver guard, so it would have registered handlers that panic on first use — it is now appended by concrete type only when non-nil.

title: idegateway: a complete second ContextVM dispatch stack that no production event reaches
description:
Code: S7/S4 (structural, dead duplicate). Files: internal/idegateway/handler.go:161-175, 276-331, 631-712; types.go:99-110.
Evidence: HandleEvent has 'case KindContextVM: return h.handleContextVMEvent(...)', which builds a THROWAWAY contextvm.NewRouter() per inbound event (:290), re-registers handlers, dispatches, then hand-rolls the response event (sign + e/p tags + publish) in publishContextVMResponse using a forked JSONRPCResponse/RPCError envelope with "2.0" hardcoded. But ingest/processor.go:339 routes eventkind.ContextVM to the SHARED contextVMRouter and :341 hands idegateway only eventkind.IDESession; cmd/drydock/main.go:737 registers IDE methods on the shared router. Verified: the case KindContextVM branch is unreachable in production. publishReviewResponse (:631) is reached only from publishErrorResponse (:668, zero callers) and handler_test.go:265.
Correct shape: delete the case KindContextVM arm, handleContextVMEvent, publishContextVMResponse, publishReviewResponse, publishErrorResponse, and the JSONRPCResponse/RPCError types. The live path is already contextvm.Router + Transport.SendResponseToEvent (transport.go:150), which builds the identical e/p-tagged 25910 response.
Cost: two response encoders for one wire format, already diverged — the dead one emits session/request/fix tags, the live one does not, so a reader concludes IDE clients receive correlation tags they never get. ~150 lines of signing-and-publishing kept green by tests.
close_reason: Fixed: deleted the unreachable case KindContextVM arm, handleContextVMEvent, publishContextVMResponse, publishReviewResponse, publishErrorResponse, and the forked JSONRPCResponse/RPCError types (~170 lines). ingest.Processor routes kind-25910 to the shared contextvm.Router; idegateway now handles only kind-30078. Deleted TestPublishReviewResponseUsesContextVMJSONRPC (tested the removed encoder); retargeted the ReviewRequest/FixRequest decode tests at contextvm.ParamsAs, the production path. Also deleted the 7 zero-reference compat aliases, HandledKinds/IsHandled/IsIDEEvent, and ParseReviewRequest/ParseFixRequest.

title: repositoryRefFromPatch duplicated byte-for-byte in ingest and revieworder
description:
Code: S4 (drift, security boundary). Files: internal/ingest/processor.go:479-499 vs internal/revieworder/service.go:503-523.
Evidence: identical function including the error string 'patch must contain exactly one canonical 30617 repository address' and the hardcoded '30617:' prefix. Both packages already import internal/scope and both call scope.ParseRepositoryRef.
Correct shape: scope.RepositoryRefFromTags(tags nostr.Tags) (RepositoryRef, error) next to ParseRepositoryRef, built from scope.RepositoryAnnouncementKind instead of the literal. Both call sites shrink to one line. scope imports only nostr/nip19, so no cycle.
Cost: Drydock's definition of 'which repository does this patch belong to' — a security boundary, since it gates monitoring scope — lives in two files that must be edited together with no compiler or test linking them.
close_reason: Fixed: added scope.RepositoryRefFromTags(nostr.Tags) built from RepositoryAnnouncementKind instead of the '30617:' literal, plus scope.ErrAmbiguousRepositoryRef. Deleted both byte-identical repositoryRefFromPatch copies from internal/ingest/processor.go and internal/revieworder/service.go; both call sites are now one line. 'strings' dropped from processor.go as it became unused.

title: publisher: init() panics comparing compile-time constants, plus a runtime guard on a constant assignment
description:
Code: S1 (confidence). Files: internal/publisher/status.go:295-306, internal/publisher/service.go:170-181.
Evidence: status.go has 'func init() { if nostr.KindStatusOpen != 1630 { panic(...) } ... }' — three runtime panics comparing typed compile-time consts to literals. The compiler folds every one to false before the binary exists. service.go:170 assigns summaryEvent = nostr.Event{Kind: nostr.KindComment, ...} and then nine lines later checks 'if summaryEvent.Kind >= 1630 && summaryEvent.Kind <= 1633 { return error }' on a field never touched in between.
Correct shape: delete both. If a real guard is wanted it is a compile-time assertion (const _ = uint(nostr.KindStatusOpen - eventkind.StatusOpen)), which fails the build rather than the process.
Cost: a panic path in a long-running relay service for an unreachable condition, plus false confidence — it reads as protection against library drift while proving nothing a go build would not. The service.go check also embeds 1630-1633 as literals (see the eventkind issue).
close_reason: Fixed: replaced status.go's init() panics with compile-time const assertions (both directions, so a drift in either fails the build rather than the process). Deleted service.go's runtime 'Kind >= 1630 && Kind <= 1633' guard on a field assigned nostr.KindComment as a constant nine lines earlier, replacing it with a comment.

title: publisher: the package that emits every event does not use the eventkind registry
description:
Code: C1 (drift). Files: internal/publisher/service.go:179,348,379,385; audit.go:16-18; status.go:222,296-306; fix_patch.go:124; security_audit.go:343-344,363,442,445.
Evidence: internal/publisher does not import internal/eventkind at all (verified: only listener, marketplace, ingest, idegateway, monitoring, contextvm, pipeline do). It hardcodes target.Kind == 1619, scope.RootKind = 1618, Kind >= 1630 && Kind <= 1633, KindCASAudit nostr.Kind = 4903, KindClientAuthentication nostr.Kind = 22242, and '30617:' / {"K","30617"} in five places.
Correct shape: eventkind.GitPullRequestUpdate (1619), eventkind.GitPullRequest (1618), eventkind.StatusOpen..StatusDraft (1630-33) all already exist in internal/eventkind/kinds.go. nostr.KindClientAuthentication is already 22242 in the pinned library — delete the local redeclaration. Add CASAudit = 4903 to the registry. For the repo address use scope.RepositoryRef.Address or one repoAddressTag(repoID) helper.
Cost: the registry's stated purpose ('centralizes the Nostr event kinds consumed by Drydock') is defeated at the one package that WRITES events. A NIP renumbering updates every consumer and silently misses every producer.
close_reason: Fixed: internal/publisher now imports internal/eventkind. Added eventkind.CASAudit = 4903 to the registry; publisher.KindCASAudit is now an alias of it. Replaced the local KindClientAuthentication redeclaration with the library's nostr.KindClientAuthentication, target.Kind == 1619 with eventkind.GitPullRequestUpdate, and scope.RootKind = 1618 with eventkind.GitPullRequest. The five '30617' repo-address literals now go through repositoryAddress()/repositoryAnnouncementKindString built from scope.RepositoryAnnouncementKind. Remaining 1630-1633 literals are in doc comments and in the compile-time assertion that deliberately pins the literal against the library constant.

title: Reject symlinked snapshot storage roots during restore and mutable reads
description: workspacesnapshot.Manager.Restore validates storagePath lexically and reads descriptor.json/patch without rejecting symlink components. Mutable Snapshot.ReadFile rejects symlinks below filesRoot but does not Lstat filesRoot itself. Content hashes still fail closed, so this is defense-in-depth/TOCTOU hardening rather than a current arbitrary-read release blocker. Harden restored snapshot storage so root, descriptor, patch, and files root cannot be symlink redirected.
acceptance_criteria: Restore and subsequent mutable reads reject symlinked storage directories, descriptor/patch entries, filesRoot, and component swaps; regression tests cover each case without weakening manifest/hash verification.

title: Expand pinned-review snapshots beyond changed-file-only allowlists
description: Pipeline agentic preparation freezes pinned Git snapshots with Allowlist set only to analysis.ChangedFiles. The discovery/reviewer tools therefore cannot inspect unchanged dependencies, callers, or related tests even though the plan's agentic discovery loop is intended to explore the repository. This is a review-depth limitation rather than a release correctness/security blocker; define a bounded, policy-aware repository scope that permits relevant unchanged-file reads without broadening access outside the frozen commit.
acceptance_criteria: Pinned pipeline reviews can read policy-authorized unchanged files from the frozen commit; exclusions remain enforced; tests prove changed files plus relevant unchanged dependencies are visible while excluded/out-of-scope paths remain denied.

title: Preserve highest canonical priority during ensemble consensus
description: reviewengine mergeFindings selects the representative same-key finding solely by confidence before assigning canonical priority. A higher-confidence lower-severity member can therefore replace a P0/P1 finding and downgrade the consensus result. Consensus should retain the highest canonical priority while still applying the intended confidence aggregation and deterministic representative selection.
acceptance_criteria: Tests with matching findings of different priorities and confidences prove consensus cannot downgrade the highest canonical P0/P1 priority; representative selection remains deterministic.
notes: Fixed in 7377fef: consensus and nearby dedup preserve the highest canonical priority while retaining the highest-confidence representative.
close_reason: Canonical priority can no longer be downgraded by confidence.

title: Short-circuit continuations for broken review sessions
description: After snapshot verification marks a review session broken, a retry of Continue currently resolves and verifies the corrupt snapshot again and returns ErrHashMismatch instead of honoring the persisted StateBroken state. Check terminal/broken state before repeating snapshot resolution so retries fail deterministically with ErrBroken and do not touch the model.
acceptance_criteria: After one corrupt-snapshot continuation marks a session broken, subsequent continuation attempts return ErrBroken without invoking snapshot loading/verification or the LLM.
notes: Fixed in 7377fef: Continue checks persisted broken/expired state before snapshot resolution or verification; retries return ErrBroken without model execution.
close_reason: Broken sessions now short-circuit deterministically.

title: Normalize mid-loop agentic cancellation stop reason
description: When the LLM Complete call returns context.Canceled after at least one successful tool turn, internal/agenticreview.Reviewer currently reports StopTransportError. Preserve fail-closed/no-partial-review behavior, but classify cancellation consistently as StopCancelled (including errors.Is wrapping) so metrics and callers distinguish operator cancellation from transport failures.
acceptance_criteria: A focused test cancels during an iterative review after evidence collection and observes StopCancelled with no partial review; non-cancellation Complete errors remain StopTransportError.
notes: Fixed in 7377fef: wrapped mid-loop Complete/tool cancellation maps to cancelled, returns no partial review, and discovery cancellation does not enter exhaustion fallback.
close_reason: Cancellation stop reason normalized with focused regression coverage.

Startup verification — on boot (and optionally periodically), GET {BaseURL}/v1/models for each distinct endpoint and compare the served model id against the configured one; log a warning + metric on mismatch. Optional flag (e.g. DRYDOCK_MODEL_NAME_SOURCE=config|endpoint) to adopt the served id automatically.

Extend LLMClient to surface it (struct return or metadata callback) and publish exactly what served each request. Most accurate; catches gateway-level rerouting. notes: Tier 1 landed with the 1618 diff fix. Tiers 2-3 are follow-up work.
