title: pkg/*: hand-maintained converters with no parity guarantee, and a lossy streaming round-trip
description:
Code: S7 (drift). Files: pkg/codemap/codemap.go, pkg/context/context.go, pkg/repository/repository.go, pkg/review/review.go.
Evidence on existence: nothing under cmd/ or internal/ imports pkg/* (grep drydock/pkg/ outside pkg/ -> zero hits, including tests) and no .md mentions them, so they are an intended external SDK surface — that part is legitimate and is NOT the finding. Per package: pkg/repository owns real policy (root-spec validation, local-vs-managed-git dispatch, sentinel translation); pkg/review owns real policy (stream normalization, mapError's error taxonomy, provider validation); pkg/context owns one real rule (the fail-closed authoritative-tokenizer contract); pkg/codemap is a pure DTO mirror with no policy.
The shape problems:
1. mapSymbols/fromInternalMap/sourceSymbols hand-copy ~15 fields each, so internal/codemap adding a field produces NO COMPILE ERROR in pkg/codemap — the public type silently omits it. The enums are pure renames (SymbolKind(symbol.Kind)) where Go type ALIASES would make the packages share the definition. Correct shape: type aliases for the identical enums (zero-cost, removes the cast layer) plus a compile-time parity guard (a var _ = internalcodemap.Symbol{...all fields...} exhaustiveness check). Full codegen is NEEDS REVIEW — heavier than the problem.
2. pkg/review/review.go:390-432 + 244-266: for a StreamingProvider, events travel pkg.Event -> streamingCompletionAdapter goroutine -> reviewengine.CompletionStreamEvent -> reviewengine.StreamCompletion (which for a streaming client just returns the channel unchanged, stream.go:49-51) -> normalizeStream goroutine -> pkg.Event. The two enum sets are 1:1 identical. The round-trip is NOT lossless: mapping EventCompletion copies only event.Result.Model (:411-414), and normalizeStream emits content.String() from accumulated deltas (:475) — so a provider that streams no deltas and returns full text in the terminal Result.Content (the DOCUMENTED shape, :167) yields Result.Content == "". Correct shape: feed a StreamingProvider's channel to normalizeStream directly with a small adapter reading Result.Content into the accumulator; keep the reviewengine hop only for the non-streaming fallback. Deletes ~45 lines, one goroutine, one channel.
3. pkg/review/review.go normalizeStream sends on out with a BARE 'out <- Event{...}' while the upstream adapter 30 lines above carefully wraps every send in select{case out<-mapped: case <-ctx.Done(): return}. A consumer who cancels and stops draining blocks the normalizer goroutine forever holding the accumulated content builder — a leak that only manifests under cancellation, i.e. in production shutdown paths, never in tests. Correct shape: apply the identical select guard to every send in normalizeStream and emitTerminal.
Cost: every internal type extension requires remembering a manual converter edit, with a silently stale public API as the failure mode.

title: Assorted single-package shape fixes found during the audit
description:
Code: mixed (load/cosmetic). Grouped because each is a small local edit.
- internal/contextbuilder/workspace.go:115-140: a hand-rolled YAML parser with the comment 'Simple YAML parsing for packages list — avoids a YAML dependency.' The comment is FALSE: gopkg.in/yaml.v3 is a direct require (go.mod:16) already used by internal/repoconfig. It handles only a top-level packages: key with '- item' children, missing flow sequences (packages: ['a/*']), nested keys and multi-document files, so valid pnpm workspaces are silently treated as single-package repos with no error path. Correct shape: yaml.Unmarshal into struct{ Packages []string  }.
- internal/agenttools/selection.go:567-589,465-467,617-620: coalesceRanges/subtractRange/effectiveTokenLimit/selectionHash are verbatim copies of contextselection.CoalesceRanges/SubtractRange/EffectiveTokenLimit/Hash — and agenttools ALREADY IMPORTS contextselection and already converts its LineRange field-by-field (:499-505). Already drifted: the exported version defensively copies before sorting, the agenttools copy sorts the caller's slice in place, so Selection.Add mutates its argument's order.
- internal/agenttools/handlers.go:391-397 syntheticSnapshotPatch fabricates a fake unified diff from a []string of paths purely so the providers accept it; SecuritySurfaceProvider.Build then parses that fake diff and pickPaths it straight back into []string — the type it wanted. Correct shape: add Files []string to SecurityTraceRequest/LayerFacade.Analyze's input; delete syntheticSnapshotPatch. Paths with spaces silently mis-parse.
- internal/codemap/graph.go:154-222 vs internal/contextbuilder/search.go:44-200: two implementations of 'grep a symbol: prefer ripgrep, fall back to git grep -P then -F, parse file:line:text'. Already differ — Searcher caps --max-count=50 and strips the repo prefix, codemap does neither; codemap uses strconv.Atoi, Searcher uses fmt.Sscanf with the error discarded. Correct shape: contextbuilder.Searcher is already exported; add a Ref option for codemap's git grep <ref> need and delete codemap.searchSymbol/gitGrepSymbol/parseCallsites. No cycle.
- Two 'is this a test file?' predicates in the SAME package with divergent rules: internal/contextbuilder/impact_provider.go:409-422 isTestPath (lowercases, matches _test. any language, /test/ anywhere) vs tool_facades.go:102-110 isTestFile (case-sensitive, requires exactly _test.go, /test/ only in the dir part); search.go:132-141 testGlobs is a third. So store_test.rb / Foo_Test.go / spec/foo.py are tests to one layer and not to the other.
- internal/contextbuilder/builder.go:129-130: exported QdrantClient any / EmbedClient any fields documented as functional with ZERO readers and ZERO writers repo-wide; the real wiring is WithQdrant/WithChartRoom. A caller doing BuilderOptions{QdrantClient: c} gets no retrieval and no error.
- internal/contextbuilder/nostr_protocol_provider.go:1-25 NostrProtocolProvider has zero registrations (auditengine and securityreview call knowledge.ReviewerSystemPreamble() directly); analysis.go:67-70 AnalyzePatchFiles is called only from the tautological facade test. Delete both and LayerNostrProtocol.
- KLUDGE-02: facades.go:57-63,:90-96 and builder.go:369-383 recover structured data by RE-PARSING markdown the same package just rendered (strings.Cut then split 'symbols: a, b'; scan lines for TestCoverageGapPrefix twice). The producers hold syms and uncovered as []string and throw them away into a string. The codebase already knows this is wrong — ContextBundle.ChangedFiles' comment (builder.go:71) says 'This is authoritative and should be used instead of scraping the rendered bundle content.' Correct shape: return the slices alongside the content. Today a symbol name containing ', ' silently empties the list.
- internal/conversation/handler.go:168,178,208,216,230,249,253,260: MarkConversationFailed's return value discarded at EIGHT sites while :241-244 in the same function handles it properly with errors.Join. A failed mark leaves the turn non-terminal forever and the retry sweep never sees it. Correct shape: one failTurn helper containing the :241-244 body.
- internal/securityscan/dedup.go:102-105 and reviewengine/ensemble.go:357-360,420-423: three copies of 'if normalized, err := NormalizeFindings(result); err == nil { return normalized }; return result' — the un-normalized slice is returned with the error dropped, so a malformed finding fails much later at normalizeReviewerExecution or Validate with an error naming the wrong stage. In securityscan's case it is PUBLISHED, because runner.go:810 has no error path.
- internal/agenticreview/reviewer.go:560 wraps Snapshot.Verify() with %v while :97 wraps the same call with %w, flattening workspacesnapshot.ErrHashMismatch — which recordSnapshotCorruption (service.go:657-661) exists solely to errors.Is against. So snapshot corruption at reviewer-execution time is invisible to the metric built to count it. Same flattening at reviewer.go:316,323,352,392,410,426,492,566,570 and service.go:626,629. Go 1.20+ supports multiple %w and this module is go 1.26.
- internal/reviewengine/client.go:147 uses a bare type assertion for *LLMHTTPError instead of errors.As, and :151 uses err == context.Canceled instead of errors.Is; IsTransient's default (:156) is true, so once any middleware wraps with %w a 400 Bad Request falls to the default and is retried three times with backoff.
- internal/agenticreview/service.go:440: 'target, _ := json.Marshal(state.envelope)' discards the error on the target-identity envelope then persists it (:448); every other marshal in the file checks. A failure writes an empty TargetEnvelope and Continue's VerifyMaterials either passes vacuously or fails naming the wrong cause.
- internal/securityreview/stage.go:28-34,82: Run returns only SecurityResult with the error carried as result.Error, so errors.Is/As cannot traverse it and a future caller who forgets the field check gets no vet signal. securityverify.Engine.Run, called from inside this very function at :154, already returns ([]Finding, error).
- internal/codechat/handler.go:46-52,293-298: Keyer.Decrypt is declared and NEVER called; decryptDM decrypts nothing (it checks event.Kind and returns event.Content verbatim). The name asserts a security property the function does not provide, so a reader auditing DM confidentiality stops there.
- internal/conversation/handler.go:235-256 runs raw SQL through h.store.DB() for the staging transition while calling h.store.SetConversationResponse three lines later for the terminal one. The conversations schema's column names now live in two files and a migration touching db/schema.go will not surface this statement.
- internal/metareview/service.go:512-533 changedLineSet matches rows starting with + or -, which includes the '+++ b/foo.go' and '--- a/foo.go' FILE HEADERS. reviewengine.sanitizeSuggestedDiff (types.go:350-355) gets this right with HasPrefix exclusions. File-header strings enter the Jaccard key used by FindReusableMetaReview against MinReuseJaccard, inflating similarity between any two patches touching the same filenames — so meta-reviews get reused across substantively different diffs.
- internal/nostrscan/detector.go:416-430,486-498: hasWord calls regexp.MustCompile on EVERY invocation (7x per eventTypeRE hit per file) and findMessageVerbs compiles six regexes per file — on a whole-tree scanner handling up to 32MB. The same file already has the correct pattern in a package-level var block at :292-298.
- internal/health/server.go:40,259-264: the database bypasses the package's own readiness-check registry with a special-cased db field and a hand-built componentStatus, and reports 'not_ready' where every other dependency reports 'degraded' — so a monitoring rule keyed on degraded misses every database outage. Correct shape: _ = s.AddReadinessCheck("database", db) in New.
- internal/circuitbreaker/breaker.go:41-55,59-66,85-96: four default values written out three times (doc comments, DefaultConfig(), and New()'s zero-value fallbacks). Correct shape: New merges against DefaultConfig() and the comments say 'see DefaultConfig'.
- internal/metrics/metrics.go:325-578: writeMetrics is a 253-line hand-maintained parallel registry where each of 95 metrics appears twice. Currently complete — no drift yet — but adding a metric needs two coordinated edits with nothing to catch the second being forgotten; the new var compiles, is incremented, and never reaches /metrics. Correct shape: self-registration at declaration + a loop. (Keeping the package dependency-free is a legitimate trade-off and is NOT the finding.)
- internal/repo/manager.go:759-838: runGitNULCountLimited and runGitStdoutLimited share a 12-line prologue, an identical Wait/error epilogue, and FOUR copies of '_ = cmd.Process.Kill(); _ = cmd.Wait()'; only the read loop differs. Correct shape: startGit(...) + killAndReap(cmd). Also :480-483 EnsureCommitAvailable runs 'git cat-file -e' a fourth time to decide whether to error, under a mutex held since :453, when every path reaching it has just run the same command and seen it fail.
- internal/betterleaks/provider.go:15-27 Provider.Build returns in.SecretScanContext — a field of its own input, already rendered by FormatContext at pipeline/runner.go:563. A type, constructor, three interface methods and a main.go registration to express 'pass this string through'. Relatedly securityscan.Provider forces securityscan->contextbuilder, which is the only reason Location/Result were exiled to the 19-line securityscan/surface package, while six sibling providers live inside contextbuilder.
- internal/betterleaks/scanner.go:243-257 parseReport hand-rolls 'decode one JSON array then require EOF' in 15 lines; json.Unmarshal already rejects trailing data. internal/driftguard/guard.go:56-62 re-indents stored JSON via map[string]any -> MarshalIndent, reordering keys alphabetically and rendering all numbers as float64, so the drift sample a human reads is not the response the model produced; json.Indent preserves it.
- internal/auditengine/engine.go:59-70: Budget{20, 16_000, 1, false, "high"} — unkeyed literals for a 5-field struct, so reordering or inserting a field silently rewrites the three numbers that bound every audit's cost.
- internal/securityscan/rules.go:90-95 hasExtension is strings.HasSuffix with a redundant length guard and no lowercasing, so .GO/.TS files are silently skipped while its sibling symbols.LangFromExt lowercases. rules.go:14 SURFACE-ENTRY matches only Go and Python main/handler — no fn main (Rust), no public static void main (Java), no int main( (C) — although internal/symbols parses function declarations in all of those and nostrscan explicitly targets .rs; auditengine/engine.go:283 already has the *codemap.Map in hand before calling LocateSurface at :291.
- internal/repoconfig NostrConfig.Enabled is a string tri-state auto|true|false — the only non-bool Enabled in the package — validated in three places and hand-decoded in two more as '!= "false" && != ""'. NO consumer distinguishes true from auto: all three gate on != "false" and then still require profile.IsNostr, so the documented 'force on' state does nothing. Correct shape: collapse to bool, or implement forcing once as a method honored at engine.go:275.
- internal/agenticreview/service.go:346-363 vs reviewer.go:487-500 duplicate the snapshot line-bounds check (including the subtle 'len(content)==0 -> lineCount=0' invariant), and for a snapshot-scope agentic review BOTH fire on the same finding. service.go:368-376 vs :378-381 repeat the identical six-field NewReviewer literal 8 lines apart. service.go:451-471 releases its lease with four scattered Release calls while Prepare, 200 lines earlier in the same file, uses a keepLease+defer idiom.

- internal/contextvm/transport.go:36-47,66-80,111-125,152-170,199-210: NewTransport accepts nil pool and nil signer, so four methods each re-run the same pool==nil/signer==nil/len(writeRelays)==0 preflight — and they have already drifted (Notify accepts per-call relays, the others do not). Correct shape: NewTransport returns an error and validates once.
- internal/publisher/service.go:407 dedupeNonEmpty and relay_publisher.go:181 dedupeRelayURLs are both in package publisher and both normalize a relay slice; Service.resolveRelays calls the first and hands the result to Publish, which IMMEDIATELY RE-DEDUPES it with the second. contextvm/audit.go:314 is a third copy.

- internal/publisher/fix_patch.go:126 writes {"t","drydock-autofix"} and internal/ingest/processor.go:526-533 hasAutofixTag re-types the same literal in a different package with no shared constant. The consumer's own comment names the stake: loop suppression. A rename on the producer side means Drydock publishes an autofix patch, ingests it, and reviews its own output recursively.
- internal/publisher/audit.go:36-49,57-59: NewAuditPublisher returns nil when signer/relayPublisher/relays are missing and Publish opens with 'if p == nil { return nil }', so a misconfigured relay list and a deliberately disabled audit trail are indistinguishable and both silent — for the compliance artifact recording every event this service signed.

Constructing a Processor without zap receipts silently disables ContextVM addressing enforcement, so kind-25910 events for OTHER recipients get dispatched to live handlers. Production is saved only because main.go:328-345 happens to always call it. Correct shape: split into WithServiceIdentity and WithZapReceipts.

title: Propagate per-response served model into RunOutput for exact review labels
description: ModelIdentity (registry keyed by baseURL+credential+configured model) resolves published labels to the last-observed served model. Under multi-model gateways, load balancing, or rolling deployments, concurrent reviews can observe different served models and the registry's last-write value may mislabel an individual review. Fix by carrying the chat-completion response's 'model' field through the LLMClient result into reviewengine.RunOutput and publishing that request-specific value; keep ModelIdentity for startup diagnostics/fallback. Requires changing the LLMClient interface signature across wrappers (Retrying/CircuitBreaking), fakes, and callers (engine, ensemble, conversation, codechat, metareview, promptrefine).
close_reason: ChatCompletion now returns ChatResult{Content, Model}; the reviewer's per-response served model flows into RunOutput.ServedModel (single-run and ensemble paths) and the runner publishes it, falling back to registry/config resolution only when the provider omits the model field.

title: upstream: fiatjaf.com/nostr writeJSONString trips -race checkptr in event Sign/SetID
description: fiatjaf.com/nostr @v0.0.0-20260611214214-c4534c716026 (the version cascadia-go v0.8.0 pins) uses uintptr pointer arithmetic in its JSON-string fast path: 'base := uintptr(unsafe.Pointer(unsafe.StringData(s)))' then '*(*uint64)(unsafe.Pointer(base + uintptr(i)))' (event.go writeJSONString, ~line 241). This violates Go's unsafe.Pointer rules and trips -race's checkptr instrumentation ('fatal error: checkptr: pointer arithmetic result points to invalid allocation') on every Event.Sign/SetID call. Affects all packages that sign events under -race (signing, publisher, payment, listener, marketplace, etc.). Production is unaffected (checkptr only enabled under -race). The newer upstream 20260716 still has the pattern. Discovered during DRYDOCK-rsa (dep migration off the local nostrlib mirror, whose older 20260320 snapshot predated this optimization). Mitigation applied: CI -race job runs with -gcflags=all=-d=checkptr=0 (data-race detection preserved). Fix path: report upstream to fiatjaf/nostr to guard the fast path behind a build tag or use unsafe.Add/unsafe.Slice correctly; remove the checkptr workaround from ci.yml once fixed. Category: reliability/observability (upstream).
